item.title: De mi script a mi propio paquete - R-Ladies Xalapa
item.description:
Chapter: R-Ladies Xalapa

When: Saturday, October 31, 2026 at 11:00 PM UTC

Where: Leonardo Pasquel 22

Attendees: 7 going

**De mi script a mi propio paquete: diseñando herramientas reproducibles en R** 📦✨ ¿Alguna vez escribiste un script para resolver un problema muy específico y después pensaste que podría servirle a alguien más? En esta sesión de RLadies+ Xalapa exploraremos cómo ese código que nació para salir del paso puede convertirse en una herramienta reutilizable, documentada y reproducible. Será una charla-demostración muy accesible en la que construiremos juntas un mini ejemplo. Partiremos de unas pocas líneas de código, las convertiremos en una función y recorreremos los elementos básicos para transformarla en un pequeño paquete de R, incluyendo su documentación y una prueba sencilla. Después conoceremos **rbims**, un paquete desarrollado para el análisis de datos metagenómicos, como ejemplo real de cómo este mismo proceso puede crecer hasta convertirse en una herramienta científica. No necesitas saber nada de metagenómica, porque el énfasis estará en R, la reproducibilidad y el diseño de software. 👩‍💻 **¿A quién va dirigida?** A personas con conocimientos básicos de R que nunca han desarrollado un paquete y tienen curiosidad por dar ese siguiente paso. 🧭 **¿Qué haremos?** * Una charla introductoria sobre por qué empaquetar nuestro código * Una demostración paso a paso, del script a la función y de la función al paquete * Un recorrido por rbims como caso real * Un espacio de preguntas y conversación **Facilitadora:** Dra. Mirna Vázquez Rosas Landa Te esperamos el sábado 31 de octubre de 2026 a las 17:00 horas (GMT-6). Puedes ir disfrazada🎃. **Código de conducta** Recuerda leer y atender nuestro código de conducta disponible [aquí](https://rladies.org/about-us/coc/).

item.title: posit::conf(2026) %>% glimpse() - R-Ladies+ Melbourne
item.description:
Chapter: R-Ladies+ Melbourne

When: Thursday, October 29, 2026 at 6:30 AM UTC

Where: DiUS

Attendees: 11 going

**posit::conf(2026) %>% glimpse()** **Date:** 29th October, 2026 **Time:** 5:30 PM (networking and refreshments from 5:30 PM; talk begins at 6:00 PM) **Where:** DiUS, Level 3/31 Queen St, Melbourne Curious about how involvement in open source, community building, mentoring, advocacy, or volunteering can open unexpected doors in your career? Wondering how people find their way into international conferences, scholarship opportunities, and global professional networks, and what role community participation plays along the way? Join us for a conversation with Dionne and Mansi, who attended **posit::conf(2026)** in Houston, Texas as **Opportunity Scholars**. This session is not just about the conference itself. It is about the communities, relationships, and contributions that helped make the opportunity possible. They will share their journeys through open source and community involvement, and the value of networking, building meaningful professional connections, and contributing to communities in ways that create impact for both oneself and others. Along the way, they will share some of their favourite moments from the conference, lessons from meeting people across the global data science ecosystem, and insights that stayed with them long after the conference ended. Whether you're new to the R community, considering your first conference application, interested in open source, or simply curious about building a more connected and community-focused career, we'd love to see you there!

item.title: Rainy Day Bioacoustics: Listening to Birds with R - R-Ladies Vancouver
item.description:
Chapter: R-Ladies Vancouver

When: Thursday, October 29, 2026 at 1:00 AM UTC

Where: Vancouver Public Library - Mount Pleasant Branch

Attendees: 9 going

As the Vancouver rain sets in, getting out into the field to listen to birds gets a bit trickier—but we can still tune in from the comfort of R! In this hands-on workshop, Sunny will introduce essential R packages designed for bioacousticians. We will walk through extracting bird sounds from Xeno-Canto, running machine learning models like BirdNET to detect species, and visualizing acoustic results—all within R! Along the way, we'll explore beautiful bird vocalizations and spotlight common Pacific Northwest species you hear around Vancouver, from the cheerful songs of Song Sparrows and Black-capped Chickadees to the ever-present Crows. \*\*\* 1. If this is your first R-Ladies event, please take a moment to review our R-Ladies Global code of conduct: [https://github.com/rladies/starter-kit/wiki/Code-of-Conduct](https://github.com/rladies/starter-kit/wiki/Code-of-Conduct) 2. Who is this allowed to attend the event? Everyone is welcome to join us at our events and to be a part of our mission to empower gender minorities with the skills and knowledge to code in one of the top programming language in data science, which is R. 3\. To fulfill this mission we do ask participants to respect a focus on the encouragement and support for women and non\-binary people during our events\.

Join us for a relaxed evening of learning and good company—we're hosting a peer teaching evening. In the first half you have time to explore a package of your choosing (e.g., looking at the vignette, what are the beginning functions to know). Then in the last half we'll take a round to share what we learned. You can find some inspiration for R packages here: https://medium.com/@ZhouAnnaWrites/20-useful-r-packages-you-may-not-know-about-54d57fe604f3 Whether you're a beginner looking for a nudge in the right direction or a seasoned R-user happy to share what you know, you're welcome here! The event will take place in the room ØHM11. The outer door is locked, but we will wait outside to let you in, or call me on 92076982 Mazemap: https://link.mazemap.com/E1NxhvoO Google maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/MbuZZPL8m2simBwd9 The room may be a bit confusing to find, because it is NOT in the main building of Øya helsehus, it is in a smaller building right east of it.
